articles.title: Downed power line initial response
articles.content: Treat every downed or sparking line as a life-safety incident. Keep people clear, call emergency services where needed, capture the location, and route the incident to field operations with an immediate escalation.
articles.snippet: Keep people clear and escalate a downed or sparking line.

articles.title: Public update approval during an outage
articles.content: Customer communications may prepare a plain-language outage update with the incident identifier, affected area, and next review time. A designated human approver must approve the statement before publication.
articles.snippet: Prepare updates, but require human approval before publication.

articles.title: Telemetry anomaly triage
articles.content: For a telemetry anomaly, preserve the source signal, identify the affected system and time window, compare it against open incidents, and route the event to engineering. Escalate when the anomaly affects a safety-critical system or service continuity.
articles.snippet: Preserve the signal and route system anomalies to engineering.

articles.title: Statutory clock response
articles.content: A report that starts a statutory or regulatory clock is a SEV1 incident. Preserve the source record, record the clock, route to the compliance desk, and escalate immediately. Do not allow an automated response to downgrade the severity.
articles.snippet: Statutory clocks are SEV1 and always escalate.
